The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844/ CR / 247 / 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024 pertaining to Survey No.113/1 measuring 557 Square Meters of Neraluru village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru Urban District.
A.P. No.14/2025 .2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 557 Square Meters in Survey No.113/1 of Neraluru village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The valuation of trees and structure were carried out by the Horticulture Department & Chartered Engineers and the respondent No.3 has passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.32,78,971/- in respect of 557 Square Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 13.02.2023 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5 crores per acre.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 /
CR / 247 / 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024.
.4. Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further, the respondent No.2 at page 5 of the impugned award has extracted the relevant portion of the Special Instructions to the guidance value notification bearing No. Mu / CVC /
485 / 2017-18 dated 05.12.2018 and on the basis of the aforesaid instructions the respondent No.2 has awarded 50% addition of the guidance value of Rs.1,853.22 per National Highways Authority Of India vs Reddy Muniyappa Basappa on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17706630/
2 Square Meters and arrived at Rs.2,780.22 per Square Meters and thereafter awarded statutory benefits under RFCTLARR Act along with 9% interest as provided under Section 3-H(5) of the NH Act on A.P. No.14/2025 the enhanced amount from the date of taking possession of the lands till date of deposit of the same with respondent No.3.

The respondent No.2 has completely ignored the defense taken by the petitioner and proceeded to award 50% without adjudicating whether the special instructions to the guidance value notification were applicable in the instant case or not.
There is a prima- facie error in understanding the special instructions and thus such error has resulted in patent illegality apparent on the face of the record.
Most importantly, it is reiterated that Survey No. 113 of Neraluru village is not abutting any NH/Bypass or ring road and in fact forms a part of new alignment in the project.

The issue regarding the non-applicability of 50% addition on the guidance value was clarified in the Statement of objections as well as during oral arguments but to the utter surprise of the petitioner, the contention taken by the petitioner has not been discussed at all in the A.P. No.14/2025 impugned Arbitral Award.
The respondent No.2 has conveniently chosen to ignore the defense taken by the petitioner to suit the needs of the respondent No.1.

The impugned Arbitral Award on the face of it opposed to most basic notions of law, morality and justice since the respondent No.2 has determined the market value of the subject lands giving benefit of the law,
which is not applicable for determination of the market value of the subject lands and the error consequently goes into the root of the matter rendering the Arbitral Award patently illegal.

There is no connection between observation of the respondent No.2 and the methodology adopted by the respondent No.2 for redetermining the market value rendering the impugned award completely arbitrary and illegal.

The respondent No.2 has grossly erred in not following the provisions of NH Act i.e., Section 3-G(7)
(a) Act, the substantive law while passing the impugned award which is A.P. No.14/2025 contrary to the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The respondent No.2 also failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The impugned Arbitral Award was passed on 03.10.2024.
The certified copy of the Arbitral Award was received by the petitioner on 15.10.2024.
The certified copy of the Arbitral Award was received by the petitioner on 15.10.2024.

The stipulated period of 3 months commences from 15.10.2024 and the petition is filed within 3 months from the date of receipt of the impugned Arbitral Award by the petitioner and hence, the petition is in time.

This Court has jurisdiction to try this petition since the seat of arbitration was Bengaluru city and impugned Arbitral Award was passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner Bengaluru Urban District within the jurisdiction of this Court.
Among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, the respondents 2 and 3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 247 / 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024 secured from the Arbitrator.

Point:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. Reddy Muniyappa Basappa is an owner of the property bearing Survey A.P. No.14/2025 No.113/1 measuring to an extent of 557 Square Meters of Neraluru village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020, is an admitted fact.

It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.32,78,971/-
was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation in respect of 557 Square Meters.

.10. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, he respondent No. 1 Sri. Reddy Muniyappa Basappa filed an application on 13.02.2023 before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5 crores per acre.
On the basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 247 / 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024.

The respondent No.2 in its order enhanced the compensation from Rs. 1,853.22 per Square Meters to Rs.2,780.22 per Square Meters and hence the respondent A.P. No.14/2025 No.2 redetermined the market value at 150% of the amount awarded by the respondent No.3.
.11.

In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector, Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 A.P. No.14/2025 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building.
Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing and determining the market value of the land,
namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated; or (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:

A.P. No.14/2025 "28. Parameters to be considered by Collector in determination of award -

The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first schedule.

In view of the aforesaid facts whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid A.P. No.14/2025 provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

sentences.text: The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the arbitrator applied 1.5 multiplier though the said multiplication is applicable to the land to the extent of only 5 guntas and the said multiplication is not applicable to this case as the extent of property is more than 5 guntas.

The petitioner also claimed that the Arbitrator has added 50% to the market value holding that acquired land is abutting to National Highway but the claim of the petitioner is that it is the newly formed highway on the acquired land and the land of the petitioner is acquired for formation of highway, as such, there is no possibility of abutting highway to the property of respondent No. 1.
Hence question of adding 50% of the market value of the A.P. No.14/2025 property of the petitioner does not arise.
The contention raised by the petitioner is that the market value was determined, hence special instructions for enhancement of compensation is not applicable to the property of the petitioner.

In view of these contentions the petitioner has to prove that the property of the respondent No.1 has been acquired for formation of new road and value of the property of the petitioner had been already declared.

Per contra, the respondent No. 1 has to prove that his property was abutting to the national highway prior to the acquisition of property and he is entitled for enhancement as per the special instructions as the competent authority have not declared the market value of the acquired property.
.14. As per the Gazette notification dated 05.12.2018, 1.5 multiplication is applicable only to the property that will not exceed more than 5 guntas.
The property involved in this case is almost 6 guntas, hence the said multiplication certainly not applicable to the present case on hand.

The petitioner claims that the land involved in this case is acquired for new project and there was no existing highway so that the Arbitrator can add additional 50% of compensation but there is no material such as sketch that shows the identification of property in which the project stated in the petition had been carried out.
Hence the said contention of the petitioner cannot be accepted in this case.
.16. The petitioner during the course of arguments has produced the gazette notification dated 05.12.2018 regarding the fixing of market value / guidance value.
As per the said document, the property involved in this case i.e., property in Survey No. 113/1 of Neraluru village comes under the potential Zone for which value is fixed at Rs. 75 lakhs per acre.
As per condition No. 4, in the guidance value the 50% or respective enhancement of 35, 30 or 25 percent can be added if the guidance value is not fixed.
When the guidance value is fixed, question of adding aforesaid percentages certainly does not arise.
I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 1st paragraph at page No. 3 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as acquisition of property by issuing notifications and it is simply stated that there is a discrimination in awarding the compensation and it is stated that first some claimants the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,853/- per Square Meter but in this case awarded only Rs. 2,780/- per Square Meter but the entire judgment nowhere discloses for which property and in which case the LAO had awarded compensation at Rs.2,780/- per Square Meter.
Apart from that what is the nature of property in which the LAO granted compensation of Rs. 2,780/- per Square Meter.

Even as per the guidance National Highways Authority Of India vs Reddy Muniyappa Basappa on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17706630/
7 value, there are different rates are fixed for different properties.

.18. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

.20. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the aforesaid provision of law.

The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the A.P. No.14/2025 parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO A.P. No.14/2025 has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.

Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by National Highways Authority Of India vs Reddy Muniyappa Basappa on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17706630/
8 the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.

Even there is no reasoning in the award that the LAO had not followed the aforesaid provisions and even there is no material on record to show that the Arbitrator has A.P. No.14/2025 gone through the award passed by the LAO and modified or enhanced the compensation.
.19. It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the A.P. No.14/2025 parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.
The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.
When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.
The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO A.P. No.14/2025 has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.

In the result following.
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.
Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB /
NH-844 / CR / 247/ 2022- 23 dated 03.10.2024 pertaining to Sy. No.113/1 measuring 557 Sq.
A.P. No.14/2025 Meters Sq. feet of Neraluru village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
